Agentic engineering? Vibe coding? Here’s what nobody tells you.

#ai #tech #aitools #aiagents #career
What nobody tells you about vibe coding. Well, we don't really call it vibe coding anymore. It's more fashionable to call it agentic engineering. But yes. Number one, you need to do the work before the build. The reason why most people fail is that they haven't really thought through what it is that they're building yet. If you don't even know what you're building, how do you expect your AI to know what you're building? The clearer your idea, the better the outcome. Two, expect things to break and know what to do. This is normal and part of the development process. Systematically debug and test as you're building. Three, build with structure, not just vibes. Think about how you're building, not just what you're building. Creating a good agentic engineering system, with things like skills, MCPs, and metaprompts, allows you to build sustainably and move faster.

instagram.author: simplifyai.mm
instagram.body:
Your agent makes decisions you can’t explain.
.
Your AI agent just took an action.
You have no idea why it chose that. ❌

Can’t debug it. Can’t fix it.
Because the reasoning is invisible.

Here is the pattern that changes this. 👇

Most agents are a prompt and a loop.
Input → ??? → Output.
Nothing visible in between.

The fix is called ReAct.
Reason. Act. Observe.

Before every action the agent writes
out its reasoning.
Why it is taking this step.
What it expects to happen.

Now you can read it.
You can see exactly where it broke.
Fix the right thing.
Not the whole system.
The exact step that failed.

REASON → ACT → OBSERVE → REPEAT
Every decision logged. Nothing hidden.

That is the difference between
a demo agent and a production agent.

💾 Save this — next time your agent
breaks you will know exactly where to look.

No hype. Real systems. 🚀

#AIEngineering #AIAgents #ReAct
#BuildWithAI #simplifyai AgenticAI

instagram.author: nathanbarry
instagram.body:
The gap between how beginners and professionals use AI is wild.

Beginners use it straight out of the box. They type a generic prompt and get a generic result. Professionals are building custom agents that complete entire workflows for them.

It’s the same tool. The difference is in how you use it.
AI beginner versus pro. The difference between the beginners and the professionals is the beginners use it just straight out of the box. They ask a simple prompt and they get a simple answer back. The professionals are using agents where they're setting up an agent or a project that is specific to an outcome or a skill that they want and they're using that over and over again. And then they're even having one agent check the other agent's work, and that allows each AI to specialize and get the highest quality output.

What nobody tells you about vibe coding. Well, we don't really call it vibe coding anymore. It's more fashionable to call it agentic engineering. But yes. Number one, you need to do the work before the build. The reason why most people fail is that they haven't really thought through what it is that they're building yet. If you don't even know what you're building, how do you expect your AI to know what you're building? The clearer your idea, the better the outcome. Two, expect things to break and know what to do. This is normal and part of the development process. Systematically debug and test as you're building. Three, build with structure, not just vibes. Think about how you're building, not just what you're building. Creating a good agentic engineering system, with things like skills, MCPs, and metaprompts, allows you to build sustainably and move faster.
